C-ROOT-WINDOW-3.IntentSummary:
Author the execution for the approved, fingerprinted spec `.ngrace/changes/active/C-ROOT-WINDOW-3/spec.xml` and only within it; the plan conforms to the spec, it does not extend, narrow or reinterpret it. The three resolved `Clarifications` (`INV-ROOT-WINDOW-UNMOVED`, `INV-ROOT-WINDOW-ROUNDING`, `INV-ROOT-WINDOW-MODE-CEILING`) are the maintainer's rulings and stand as written; this bundle implements none of them — every behaviour they resolved is already delivered at the spec's base `58e1d9e681b8bc7c794af586f7234f2c5dced3ef`, and the plan's task is to verify that end state, not to re-perform it. This bundle writes no engine, suite, fixture, registry or record byte; its close's `--retire` is a no-op (`moved 0`, driven). Planned reds: none.
Why one task and not two. The bundle performs no write, so there is nothing to decompose: a second task would be a decomposition of nothing. The single task `T-001` is verification-only — it runs the shipped instruments, records its cursor events, and reaches a boundary where every criterion the close will evaluate is already observed green. (The ngrace-plan skill does not say a plan's tasks may be verification-only; this bundle's spec is the authority that makes it so, and `C-CITATION-ANCHOR-REPAIR-2`'s archived plan is the house precedent for the shape.)
The scopes, stated with their reasons and checked against the shipped predicate. `DurableScope` is `<None />`: the spec's `AffectedAreas` names no module (measured — its section is prose), the engine and its suite sit under `scripts/`, which is lint-ignored (`.ngrace-lint.json` `ignoredDirs`), and no module in `.ngrace/graph/main.xml` owns any record file; do not mint a synthetic module. `ObservedWriteScope` is `<None />` because the task writes no file: the observed scope lists observed task writes, and no task below performs any write. The executor's own cursor events and the CLI's command-run records live under this bundle's own directory and are not task writes (the same reading the predecessor's close passed under). The empty marker is the shipped accepted form — prose such as "none" is invalid, the `<None />` element is required, and the lint run at this plan's commit accepts it (measured, exit 0). `isModuleOwnableWritePath` (`src/lint/core.ts:732`) returns false for every path outside `src/`, so `change.graph-anchors-miss-write-scope` cannot fire for an empty anchor set.
The mapping, fixed by the spec's own Constraint (the trap that has cost supersedes): exactly one criterion — `AC-NO-CURRENT-MODE` — carries no `CloseEvidence` and is mapped by exactly one task `Satisfies`, carried by `T-001` below; it is this plan's only `Satisfies`, and no other task carries one (there is no other task). Measured basis at this plan's commit: `validateSpecPlanCoverage` (`src/artifact/grammar.ts:1981`) warns `change.acceptance-criterion-unmapped` for a criterion that is neither task-mapped nor close-bound, `isCloseBoundCriterion` (`src/artifact/grammar.ts:2142`) counts a criterion close-bound when it carries a complete `CloseEvidence` child, and `change.close-evidence-and-satisfied` (`src/lint/catalog.ts:286`) errors on a `Satisfies` of a close-bound criterion; eleven of this spec's twelve criteria are close-bound and `AC-CLOSE-LINT`'s `CloseEvidence` runs `--fail-on warnings`, which fails on any issue, so an unmapped `AC-NO-CURRENT-MODE` would make the bundle's own close unsatisfiable. `AC-CLOSE-LINT` stays the close's: its command appears in no task `Verification` and in no `TargetAssertions` entry. Every `CloseEvidence` is evaluated only in the applied-archive state (F196's rule).
The fix budgets, stated because they bind the task (`FIX_SIGNATURE_REPEAT_BUDGET = 2`, `FIX_DISTINCT_SIGNATURE_BUDGET = 4`, `src/grace-cursor.ts:187` and `:193`, re-read at this plan's commit). With no write there is no fix loop: there is no file a fix could edit, so neither budget can be exercised. A failed verification cycle here would mean a criterion that is false at the baseline — the end state the spec asserts does not hold — and the only honest response is a stop and a report, never a fix. The budgets are recorded so the accounting is explicit, not because this bundle expects to spend them.
Why the assertions are what they are. `BaselineAssertions` pin the standing world with existence and command pins only: the seven record files, the stub and the inventory, the engine and its suite, the authorizing spec, and the four shipped instruments that are green at the baseline — measured at this plan's commit, every one exit 0 (the suite 78 pass / 0 fail / 1273 `expect()` calls; the validator, the preservation validator and the citation validator each `ok`, exit 0). `TargetAssertions` are the same set plus nothing — nothing new lands, no test is added, and no byte pin exists on any record file because this bundle writes no byte (the C-PAYMENT-RECORD-3 precedent against moving baseline byte pins). The four instruments are executed at execution time by the selected target lint's `--run-commands` path; the suite also runs directly as `T-001`'s first command. No `TargetAssertions`-bound assertion depends on a later task, because there is no later task.
Every `Verification` command recorded below, measured at this plan's commit `b4c5772` (F184's rule, refined): the suite exits 0 (78/0/1273); the four named-baseline diffs exit 0 (the tree is byte-identical to the base for every pathset — the ratchet edit, the engine, the suite, the golden capture and the record's post-move state are all inside the baseline); and the selected `bun ./src/grace.ts lint --path . --change C-ROOT-WINDOW-3 --assertions target --run-commands` command exits 1 at plan time (`assertion.change-not-approved`) because the plan is draft — which is not a defect (F184's refined rule, the same reading the predecessor's plan recorded): its meant stage is execution, after the maintainer's ratification and the gate, when spec and plan are both approved and identity-matched; driven to exit 0 in the faithful copy with the plan carried at the status that stage has. No recorded command contains a current-mode lint of this project root (F171, by hand — the shipped detector misses the `grace.ts` form): no command text contains `--assertions current`, and none invokes lint of this root omitting `--assertions`; the target lint is a selected target lint, the form the phase rules permit.
The faithful-copy law (F231), discharged at plan time. The brief's probe was driven on a faithful copy of the working tree built by `rsync` with untracked files and `.git` included (a `git clone` drops the untracked run events whose folded `WriteEvidence` the ratchet reads; `node_modules` carried so the CLI resolves): the supersede of `-2` is already committed at this HEAD, so there is nothing to supersede in the copy; `-3` archived with `status="applied"` on spec and plan; the close's `--retire` probe reporting `moved 0`, exit 0; every `CloseEvidence` command and the full `bun run validate:ci` exit 0 inside the copy in the applied-archive state. The close's measured byte table is empty for every record path: only the two `.ngrace/changes/` moves happen, and each is excluded by name in `AC-NO-ARCHIVE-EDIT` (F188's three arrivals — the row's already-archived home `C-ROOT-WINDOW`, the predecessor's supersede arrival `C-ROOT-WINDOW-2`, this bundle's own close arrival `C-ROOT-WINDOW-3`).
The close, stated once and never performed by a task. The executor emits its own execution-time cursor events for `T-001` (opened with the epoch open at the task's start, progress, attempt with signature kind and key on every failed verification cycle, verification-unavailable when evidence cannot be collected, pause and resume around interruptions) and does not omit them; command-run is produced by the CLI's `--run-commands` path, never hand-invented. The terminal event, the cursor fold, every gate, the status write, the archive move and the close's own record retirement move are close acts owned by the authority; no task performs any of them, and no sentence in this plan implies execution does. Do not hand-write any status. The byte-invariance baseline for every diff command is the spec's base commit `58e1d9e681b8bc7c794af586f7234f2c5dced3ef` (F210's rule); every diff sees tracked paths only (F174); no criterion compares a fixed `git show` against a floating working-tree read (F215); no recorded command pins a named finding `live` or a ceiling to a number, and this plan adds no test, so F185 and F213 have nothing to bind. When this plan names a tag or attribute form it writes character data with entities (`<`, `>`, `&`) and never paraphrases the brackets away.

T-001.Title: Verify the delivered end state at the baseline — run the shipped instruments, hold every byte-invariance command green, and stop at a boundary where every criterion the close will evaluate is already observed green, writing no file

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: The verification boundary. Run, in order, the six commands in `Verification` — the shipped retirement suite (78 pass / 0 fail at this plan's commit, the counts the close's `CloseEvidence` will evaluate again in the applied-archive state), the four named-baseline diffs against `58e1d9e681b8bc7c794af586f7234f2c5dced3ef` (the record files plus the stub and the inventory; `src/` and `scripts/` with no exclusions — correction 3; the archive pathset with F188's three named arrivals excluded; the README/examples/teaching/packaging surface), and the selected target lint with `--run-commands`, which evaluates this plan's `TargetAssertions` and executes their four `MustPassCommand` instruments. Every command exits 0 at the stage it runs (F184, measured at this plan's commit and re-driven inside the faithful copy); the target lint's plan-time exit 1 (`assertion.change-not-approved`, plan draft) is the refined rule's plan-time shape, not a defect. This task performs no write of any kind: no engine, suite, fixture, registry or record byte, no test added, no fixture touched, and the buffer `.ngrace/scratch/staged-findings.md` is read by no task and written by none. If any command exits non-zero at its stage, the end state is false at the baseline: stop and report — a fix is impossible by construction, because the criterion's truth was already the tree's state and no write is chartered to produce it.

The inert close and the byte-invariance boundary. This bundle's close moves its directory into `.ngrace/changes/archive/C-ROOT-WINDOW-3/` and moves nothing else: the close's `--retire` reports `moved 0` and no record byte changes (measured at this plan's commit over a record copy and again inside the faithful copy, exit 0 both), a second `--retire` likewise, and the shipped validator returns zero findings before and after. The four diff commands above are the same bytes the close's `CloseEvidence` evaluates in the applied-archive state (F196) — they are green at this plan's commit and stay green through execution because the bundle writes nothing (F174: tracked paths only; F210: the named base remains valid; F215: no fixed `git show` against a floating read). The fix budgets (`FIX_SIGNATURE_REPEAT_BUDGET = 2`, `FIX_DISTINCT_SIGNATURE_BUDGET = 4`, `src/grace-cursor.ts:187` and `:193`) bind this task and cannot be exercised: with no write there is no fix loop, and a failed verification cycle means a criterion false at the baseline — a stop and a report, never a fix.

The by-hand rule, the mapping and the boundary. No current-mode lint of this project root appears anywhere in this plan's task `Verification` commands or `TargetAssertions`, checked by hand (F171, the shipped detector missing the `grace.ts` form): no command text contains `--assertions current`, and none invokes lint of this root omitting `--assertions`; current-mode lint of this root appears only as `AC-CLOSE-LINT`'s post-archive `CloseEvidence`, owned by the authority. This task carries the plan's single `Satisfies` (`AC-NO-CURRENT-MODE`) — the mapping the close's `--fail-on warnings` requires (measured basis in IntentSummary); the close-bound criteria stay unmapped, because a `Satisfies` of a close-bound criterion is the error `change.close-evidence-and-satisfied` (`src/lint/catalog.ts:286`). The executor emits its own execution-time cursor events for this task inside the open epoch (progress, attempt with signature kind and key on fail, verification-unavailable when evidence cannot be collected) and does not omit them; the terminal event, the cursor fold, the gates, both gate verdicts, gate apply, the `status="applied"` write, gate archive, the move to `.ngrace/changes/archive/C-ROOT-WINDOW-3/`, and the close's own record retirement move are close acts owned by the authority; no task performs any of them and no sentence in this plan implies execution does. Do not hand-write any status. T-001 writes nothing: no file, in any directory, at any stage.
